title: Word and Cowork: legal plugins for Microsoft 365 Copilot add legal skills
summary: Hold: the low-cost rating and included-only licensing omit Copilot Credits consumed by Cowork skill calls. The briefing also incorrectly reports that Cowork plugin blocking and user availability have no documented automation; Microsoft provides package-management APIs for both.

claims.where: summary; Why it matters; Governance controls; controls notes
claims.claim: The Word and Cowork legal plugins have separate controls in different admin centres, rather than one plugin's control governing both.
claims.quote: Two legal plugins are available: one for Copilot in Word and one for Copilot Cowork. Each is managed differently.

claims.where: controls[0].governs; controls[0].note; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Access to the Word legal plugin is governed by a policy configuration named Legal Skills in M365 Copilot in Word.
claims.quote: Access to the plugin can be governed via the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center. Tenant admins can control access by creating a policy configuration in the Policy Management tool. The policy name is "Legal Skills in M365 Copilot in Word".

claims.where: controls[1].governs; controls[2].governs; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Access to Legal for Cowork is governed through the Microsoft 365 admin center's Agent Tools page.
claims.quote: Access to the plugin can be governed via the Microsoft 365 admin center. Tenant admins can control access via the Agent Tools page. The plugin name is "Legal for Cowork".

claims.claim: The Word control is reached in the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center through Customization > Policy Management > Policy configurations > Create > Start with the basics > Choose the scope > Configure Settings > Legal Skills in M365 Copilot in Word.
claims.quote: Under Customization, select Policy Management. On the Policy configurations page, select Create. On the Configure Settings page, select the policies that you want to include in the policy configuration.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents no PowerShell or Graph operation to configure the Cloud Policy holding the Word legal setting.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Cloud Policy service Microsoft 365 Apps policy configurations PowerShell Graph API Legal Skills in M365 Copilot in Word'; '"Cloud Policy" "API" "configuration"'. Read Cloud Policy overview and Manage Copilot for legal; no configuration call found.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance
claims.claim: A Cowork plugin can be blocked for the tenant at Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Tools > plugin > Users > Block.
claims.quote: In the Microsoft 365 admin center, select Agents > Tools. Find the plugin you want to manage and go to the Users tab. Select Block: No users in your tenant can access the plugin.

claims.claim: There is no documented API or automation for blocking the Legal for Cowork plugin.
claims.quote: A package represents an agent or a tool, such as a plugin, MCP server, or skill, in the organization catalog. Block, unblock, and reassign ownership of packages.
claims.fix: Set controls[1].api to kind 'graph', call 'POST /beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block', docs 'https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/api/admin-settings/package/copilotpackage-block'. Add to its note: 'Package Management API preview; requires a Microsoft Agent 365 licence and delegated CopilotPackages.ReadWrite.All permission; production use of beta APIs is not supported.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/api/admin-settings/package/overview for its plugin reach.

claims.where: controls[2].ui; Governance controls table; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Cowork plugin visibility can be restricted at Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Tools > plugin > Users > Available to specific users or groups.
claims.quote: In the Microsoft 365 admin center, select Agents > Tools. Find the plugin you want to manage and go to the Users tab. Available to specific users or groups: Only the users or security groups you specify can view the plugin.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents no scripted operation for the Cowork plugin's user or group availability.
claims.fix: Set controls[2].api to kind 'graph', call 'PATCH /beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}', docs 'https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/api/admin-settings/package/copilotpackagedetail-update'. Add to its note: 'The request body sets allowedUsersAndGroups and the required availableTo property; use allowedForSome for a selected audience. Package Management API preview; requires a Microsoft Agent 365 licence and delegated CopilotPackages.ReadWrite.All permission; production use of beta APIs is not supported.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/api/admin-settings/package/overview for plugin reach.

claims.claim: Learn does not establish that the Copilot package block API covers Legal for Cowork.
claims.quote: A package represents an agent or a tool, such as a plugin, MCP server, or skill, in the organization catalog. The Package Management API enables IT administrators to view and manage agents and tools across your organization.
claims.fix: Replace the automation paragraph with: 'At the time of writing (November 2026), Microsoft Learn documents no PowerShell or Graph operation for the Cloud Policy configuration. For Cowork plugins in the organization catalog, the Package Management API documents beta blocking and availability updates. These APIs require a Microsoft Agent 365 licence, and production use of beta APIs is not supported.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/api/admin-settings/package/overview and the block and update references. Manage plugins for Copilot Cowork explicitly places Cowork plugins in the Microsoft 365 app-package class.

claims.fix: Remove the 'Search the Microsoft Purview audit log for Copilot activities to see interactions with Cowork plugins' checklist bullet, which has no corresponding controls row. Keep the supported audit information in Cost and licensing.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The licensing model for the combined Word and Cowork briefing is included, with Microsoft 365 Copilot licensing as its entitlement description.
claims.quote: Cowork uses a usage-based billing model. Activities such as model responses, tool and skill calls, image generation, and browser tasks count toward your organization's consumption.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to 'mixed'. Append to licensing.notes and Cost and licensing: 'The Word legal plugin is enabled for Microsoft 365 Copilot commercial subscribers. Cowork also uses usage-based billing through Copilot Credits, including consumption from skill calls; Cowork access requires a spending policy that includes the user and selects Cowork.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/cowork/cowork-admin-governance and https://learn.microsoft.com/plugins/cost-considerations. Retain the narrower statement that Manage Copilot for legal names no separate legal-plugin price or meter.
